Dhammānuloma (1), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 4.8.
Tika Saraṇaduka (The Triplet on the Refuges)

4.8.2.1. The Tetrad of Conditions for the State of Being a Refuge (Saraṇapada Paccayacatukka) Dependent on a state that is associated with pleasant feeling and is a refuge, there arises a state associated with pleasant feeling and a refuge, by way of the root condition (hetupaccaya).

Dependent on a state associated with painful feeling that is subject to destruction, a state associated with painful feeling and subject to destruction arises by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is subject to destruction, a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling and subject to destruction arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under the root condition there are three; ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition there are three. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence and association are also the same as the section on dependence.
A state associated with pleasant feeling that is a refuge is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state associated with pleasant feeling that is a refuge.
A state associated with painful feeling that is a refuge is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state associated with painful feeling that is a refuge.

A state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) is a condition, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*), for a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is with-conflict. (Abbreviated. [In the root-condition there are] three;

in the object-condition (*ārammaṇa*), nine; in the predominance-condition (*adhipati*), five; in the proximity-condition (*anantara*) ... pe ... in the support-condition (*nissaya*), three; in the decisive-support-condition (*upanissaya*), nine; in the repetition-condition (*āsevana*), three ... pe ...
in the non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*), three. 4.8.2.2. The Section on Non-Conflict (*araṇa-pada*).

Dependent on a state associated with pleasant feeling that is free from conflict (*araṇa*), a state associated with pleasant feeling that is free from conflict arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is free from conflict, a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is free from conflict arises by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

Under the root condition, two; under the object condition, three; under the predominance condition, two ... pe ... under the repetition condition, two ... pe ... under the jhāna and path conditions, two ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition, three.
(Abbreviated. (The section on co-nascence ... pe ... and the section on association are also similar to the section on dependence.
A state associated with pleasant feeling and free from conflict is a condition, by way of the root condition, for a state associated with pleasant feeling and free from conflict.

A state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is without conflict (*araṇa*) is a condition, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*), for a state associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling that is without conflict.

(Abbreviated. [In the root-condition there are] two; in the object-condition (*ārammaṇa*), six; in the predominance-condition (*adhipati*), four; in the proximity (*anantara*) and contiguity (*samanantara*) conditions, seven;

in the conascence (*sahajāta*), mutuality (*aññamañña*), and dependence (*nissaya*) conditions, three; in the decisive support (*upanissaya*) condition, nine; in the repetition (*āsevana*) condition, two; in the kamma-condition (*kamma*), five; in the resultant (*vipāka*), nutriment (*āhāra*), faculty (*indriya*), ... [and so forth].
Three; two for jhāna and path; three for association … pe … three for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
(It should be expanded in the same manner as the Chapter on Questions in the Wholesome Triplet.

A state that is of the nature to ripen and is without conflict is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is of the nature to ripen and is without conflict … three [cases].

*Upādinnattika*, *Saraṇaduka* (The Triplet of Clung-to, the Dyad of With-Refuge).

[Three] Dependent on a state that is acquired by clinging, subject to clinging, and free from conflict, as well as a state that is not acquired by clinging, subject to clinging, and free from conflict, a state that is not acquired by clinging, subject to clinging, and free from conflict arises by way of the root condition.

(Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-condition, nine; in the case of object-condition, three; in the case of predominance-condition, five … pe … in the case of repetition-condition, two … pe … in the case of result-condition, nine … pe … in the case of non-disappearance-condition, nine. (Abbreviated.
(The section on conascent [conditions] … pe … and the section on associated [conditions] are the same as the section on dependent [conditions].

A state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, and free from conflict, is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is both clung-to and subject to clinging, and free from conflict … three.

A state that is not clung to, is subject to clinging, and is without conflict (*anupādinnupādāniyo araṇo dhammo*) is a condition, by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*), for a state that is not clung to, is subject to clinging, and is without conflict.

A state that is not clung to, is not subject to clinging, and is without conflict (*anupādinnaanupādāniyo araṇo dhammo*) is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a state that is not clung to, is not subject to clinging, and is without conflict. ... [three] (abbreviated). Under the root-condition there are seven;

under the object-condition (*ārammaṇa*), six; under the predominance-condition (*adhipati*), five ... pe ... under the support-condition (*nissaya*), eleven; under the decisive support-condition (*upanissaya*), nine.
With respect to pre-arisen [states], there are seven; with respect to post-arisen, nine; with respect to repetition, two; with respect to kamma, eight; with respect to result, six;

with respect to nutriment, twelve; with respect to faculty, jhāna, and path, seven; with respect to association, three; with respect to dissociation, ten ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance, twenty-three. (Abbreviated.

In the case of root-cause condition: one [answer] … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated.
(Also in the section on co-nascence … pe … and in the section on inquiry, it is one in every instance.

Dependent on a state that is undefiled, non-defiling, and without conflict (*araṇa*), there arises a state that is undefiled, non-defiling, and without conflict by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … three [cases].

Dependent on a state that is undefiled but defiling and without conflict, and a state that is undefiled, non-defiling, and without conflict, there arises a state that is undefiled but defiling and without conflict by way of root condition.

(Abbreviated. Under root condition there are five; under object condition two … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are five. (Abbreviated. (The section on co-nascence … pe … and the section on association are the same as the section on dependence.)

A state that is not defiled, yet subject to defilement, and free from conflict (*araṇa*), is related to a state that is not defiled, yet subject to defilement, and free from conflict, by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

A state that is not defiled, not subject to defilement, and free from conflict, is related to a state that is not defiled, not subject to defilement, and free from conflict, by way of the root condition … three [cases]. (Abbreviated.

There are four [types] for the root condition, three for the object condition (*ārammaṇa*), [and so on for] the predominance condition … four for the immediate condition (*samanantara*), five for the conascence condition (*sahajāta*).
Reciprocity: two; dependence: seven; strong-dependence: four; prenascence, postnascence, and repetition:
two; kamma …pe… path: four; association: two; dissociation: three …pe… non-disappearance: seven. (Abbreviated.

4.8.6. The Triplet on Applied Thought (Vitakkattika), the Dyad on the Objects of Refuge (Saraṇaduka).

Conditioned by a state that has applied thought and sustained thought and is an object of refuge, a state with applied thought and sustained thought that is an object of refuge arises, having a cause.

By way of root condition: dependent on a state that is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought and is a refuge, there arises a state that is without applied thought but with sustained thought and is a refuge, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought and is a refuge, there arise states that are both accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought and are a refuge, and those that are without applied thought but with sustained thought and are a refuge, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is a refuge, without applied thought but with sustained thought, there arises a state that is a refuge, accompanied by applied and sustained thought, by way of root condition.

Dependent on states that are refuges, both accompanied by applied and sustained thought and without applied thought but with sustained thought, there arises a state that is a refuge, accompanied by applied and sustained thought, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are five; ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are five. (Abbreviated.)
(Also in the section on co-nascence … and in the section on inquiry, there is a detailed exposition in all instances.

Dependent on a state that is with applied thought and sustained thought, free from conflict (*araṇa*), a state that is with applied thought and sustained thought, free from conflict, arises by way of root condition … seven.

Dependent on a state that is without applied thought and with sustained thought only, free from conflict, a state that is without applied thought and with sustained thought only, free from conflict, arises by way of root condition … five.

Dependent on a state that is without applied thought, without sustained thought, and free from conflict (*araṇa*), there arises a state without applied thought, without sustained thought, and free from conflict, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

(Abbreviated. (Abbreviated.
